# Copilot Instructions

## Build, test, and packaging commands

Use the existing GitHub Actions workflows as the source of truth.

```powershell
# Core library setup/build
dotnet workload restore src\zoft.MauiExtensions.Core\zoft.MauiExtensions.Core.csproj --ignore-failed-sources --skip-manifest-update
dotnet restore src\zoft.MauiExtensions.Core\zoft.MauiExtensions.Core.csproj --ignore-failed-sources
dotnet build src\zoft.MauiExtensions.Core\zoft.MauiExtensions.Core.csproj -c Release --no-restore

# Sample app CI build
dotnet workload restore sample\zoft.MauiExtensions.Sample\zoft.MauiExtensions.Sample.csproj --ignore-failed-sources --skip-manifest-update
dotnet restore sample\zoft.MauiExtensions.Sample\zoft.MauiExtensions.Sample.csproj --ignore-failed-sources
dotnet build sample\zoft.MauiExtensions.Sample\zoft.MauiExtensions.Sample.csproj -c Release -f net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0 --no-restore

# Local package build
dotnet build src\zoft.MauiExtensions.Core\zoft.MauiExtensions.Core.csproj -c Release

# Optional explicit pack step
dotnet pack src\zoft.MauiExtensions.Core\zoft.MauiExtensions.Core.csproj -c Release --no-build
```

```powershell
# Current test entry point
dotnet test src\zoft.MauiExtensions.sln -c Release --no-build --logger "trx;LogFileName=test_results.trx"
```

There are no dedicated test projects yet, so there is currently no single-test command. `dotnet test` is only a smoke check at the moment.

There is no separate lint command in the repository. Style/analyzer feedback comes from `.editorconfig`, `MemoryAnalyzers`, and the normal `dotnet build` pipeline.

The repository is pinned through the root `global.json` to the .NET 10.0.300 SDK, and both the library and sample target .NET 10 MAUI TFMs.

Package versioning is tag-driven through MinVer. Do not hardcode package versions in project files; release tags and `CHANGELOG.md` drive the published package version and release notes.

For a real release, push a semantic-version tag such as `5.2.0` or `5.2.0-beta.1`. `.github\workflows\publish-package.yml` validates that the generated `.nupkg` version exactly matches the tag, can push to NuGet via `workflow_dispatch`, and creates or updates the matching GitHub release on tag pushes.

Untagged local builds will produce prerelease package versions derived from the nearest semantic-version tag. `src\ReleaseNotes.g.props` is generated by the publish workflow and is git-ignored; do not edit or commit it manually.

## High-level architecture

- `src\zoft.MauiExtensions.Core` is the package that gets published. It is a multi-targeted MAUI library (`net10.0`, Android, iOS, Mac Catalyst, and Windows on Windows hosts).
- `sample\zoft.MauiExtensions.Sample` is the demo app. It references the local core project directly and acts as the main usage example for the package APIs.
- The core library is organized by feature area rather than by app layer:
  - `Models` contains the three main base types: `ZoftObservableObject`, `ZoftObservableRecipient`, and `ZoftObservableValidator`. They wrap CommunityToolkit.Mvvm types and standardize busy-state handling, disposal, and validation behavior.
  - `Services` contains localization abstractions. `ResourceManagerLocalizationService` is the main implementation.
  - `Markup` contains the `Translate` markup extension used from XAML.
  - `WeakSubscription` contains the weak-event infrastructure that prevents long-lived subscriptions from leaking viewmodels or validators.
  - `Extensions` contains the general-purpose extension methods shipped by the package.
- Localization is a cross-cutting feature that spans multiple files: the sample registers `ILocalizationService` in `MauiProgram`, the service is backed by `Localization\AppResources*.resx`, and XAML uses `{zoft:Translate Some_Key}`. The `Translate` markup extension resolves `ILocalizationService` through `ServiceHelper`, so the service must be available in DI for translated bindings to work.
- The sample app uses Shell navigation to expose one page per feature area (`DependsOn`, `Localization`, `MainThread`, `Messenger`, `Validation`, `About`). That makes the sample the best place to study intended usage before changing package APIs.

## Key conventions

- Use CommunityToolkit.Mvvm source generators, not manual property/command boilerplate. The codebase relies on `[ObservableProperty]`, `[RelayCommand]`, `[NotifyPropertyChangedFor]`, and partial property-change hooks.
- New viewmodels should usually inherit one of the `ZoftObservable*` base classes instead of the raw CommunityToolkit base classes, so they keep the shared `IsBusy` / `IsNotBusy` / `BusyMessage` and disposal behavior.
- XAML pages in the sample use compiled bindings with `x:DataType`. Preserve that pattern when editing or adding pages.
- Sample views receive their viewmodel through constructor injection in code-behind, assign `BindingContext`, and are registered as singletons alongside their viewmodels in `MauiProgram`.
- For localized UI text, prefer `{zoft:Translate ...}` in XAML and `ILocalizationService` in C# instead of reading `.resx` files directly from views.
- `ZoftObservableValidator` descendants are expected to react to validation changes by overriding `OnErrorsChanged(...)`; the base class already wires the event using weak subscriptions.
- If you add weak-event usage, keep the returned `WeakEventSubscription<...>` alive in a field and dispose it with the owning object.
- C# preview features are enabled in both projects (`LangVersion=preview`), and the repository already uses newer syntax such as primary constructors.
- The sample app uses `CommunityToolkit.Maui` 14.x because earlier 12.x releases target MAUI 9 and conflict with `Microsoft.Maui.Controls` 10.x.
- Repository style is driven by `.editorconfig`: block-scoped namespaces, `using` directives outside namespaces, CRLF line endings, 4-space indentation, and interface names prefixed with `I`.
- Public surface area in the core library is documented with XML comments and Release builds generate documentation files; avoid adding public APIs without XML docs.
- Keep `CHANGELOG.md` version headers aligned with release tags (`## [5.2.0]`, `## [5.2.0-beta.1]`, etc.), because the publish workflow extracts NuGet release notes from that exact section.
